title: Ravenhill College
victim: Professor Mortimer Hale, lecturer in literature
teaser: By college tradition, on Halloween night "The Raven" is read by candlelight in the old library. Professor Hale finished the last stanza, a draught blew out the candles, and when they were relit the professor sat dead in his armchair, with the stuffed raven from the zoology room perched on his chest. "Nevermore" was chalked on the board. The draught came from a door that had been kept locked all evening.

habits.label: Wax on the sleeve
habits.habit: Gown sleeve spattered with hardened candle wax
clues: In the old library two drops of wax have hardened on the spine of a folio lying far from the candles. The culprit has wax on their sleeve.
The rail of the bell tower's spiral stairs has white drops of candle wax, though people only go up with a lantern. The culprit has hardened wax on their sleeve.

habits.label: Chalk on the fingers
clues: In the senior common room, which hasn't a single blackboard, the door handle has white chalky fingerprints. The culprit has chalk on their fingers.
In the dean's office the telephone dial is clogged with chalk crumbs, as if the number was dialled with a dusty finger. The culprit's fingers are white with chalk.

habits.label: Feather in the hatband
habits.habit: A black feather tucked in the band of a felt hat
clues: A black feather with a trimmed quill, the kind tucked into a hatband, lies on the coat stand by the dormitory entrance. The culprit wears a feather in their hatband.
A first-year in the student club cellar remembered a hat with a black feather flashing past on the stairs. The culprit wears a black feather in their hatband.

habits.label: Skull ring
habits.habit: A silver skull ring on the ring finger
clues: In the old library an envelope lies by Hale's armchair, and a tiny skull is impressed in its sealing wax. The culprit has a skull ring.
The cleaner by the dean's office saw someone hastily turn a ring so the skull faced their palm. The culprit has a silver skull ring.

habits.label: Velvet half-mask
habits.habit: A black velvet half-mask in their pocket
clues: In the student club cellar the society's half-masks hang on hooks, and one hook holds only a broken cord. The culprit carries a velvet half-mask in their pocket.
A scrap of velvet cord with a knot like those on the society's masks was found on the bell tower stairs. The culprit has a velvet half-mask in their pocket.

habits.label: Torn hem
habits.habit: The hem of their gown is torn and pinned
clues: A black scrap with the stitched edge of a hem is caught on the hinge of the old library's locked door. The culprit's gown has a torn hem.
A safety pin with a black thread of gown cloth was found on the dormitory stairs. The culprit's gown hem is pinned up.

habits.label: Smells of formalin
clues: In the senior common room the glass stopper of the decanter smells of formalin, as if someone took it with fingers straight out of the solution. The culprit smells of formalin.
The rug on Hale's knees in the old library smells of formalin, though the stuffed raven dried out long ago and smells of nothing. The culprit smells of formalin.

habits.label: Peanuts in the pocket
habits.habit: Pockets full of roasted peanuts in their shells
clues: In the dean's office roasted peanut shells crunch under the armchair. The culprit carries peanuts in their pocket.
On the bell tower stairs a trail of peanut shells runs right up to the bell platform. The culprit's pockets are full of peanuts.

habits.label: Quotes Poe
habits.habit: Quotes Poe whether it fits or not
clues: In the dormitory someone has added a line of Poe in the margin of another student's notes: "All that we see or seem is but a dream within a dream." The culprit quotes Poe.
The canteen woman heard someone in the senior common room answer Hale in verse, and he laughed: "Your Poe again." The culprit quotes Poe whether it fits or not.

habits.label: Oar blisters
clues: In the student club cellar a plaster, the kind rowers use on blisters, is stuck to the door handle. The culprit has palms callused from the oars.
The glass door of a cabinet in the zoology room has a palm print with hard calluses at the base of the fingers. The culprit has blisters from rowing.

habits.label: Taped glasses
habits.habit: Horn-rimmed glasses with an arm wrapped in electrical tape
clues: Under the cabinet of stuffed animals in the zoology room lies a ring of black electrical tape, rolled to exactly the thickness of a glasses arm. The culprit wears glasses with a taped arm.
A courier by the dean's office remembered horn-rimmed glasses with one arm wrapped in black tape. The culprit has glasses with tape on the arm.

habits.label: Rolling R
clues: The dormitory porter heard a voice from the phone box asking for the professor and swallowing its R softly. The culprit has a guttural R.
Before the candles went out, someone whispered "bravo" from a dark corner of the old library, gargling the R. The culprit has a guttural R.

habits.label: Coffee from a flask
habits.habit: Drinks black coffee from a vacuum flask
clues: In the zoology room the marble table has a round mark from a flask and drops of black coffee. The culprit drinks coffee from a flask.
A flask cup with cold coffee at the bottom was left on the top platform of the bell tower. The culprit drinks black coffee from a flask.

habits.label: College scarf
habits.habit: A striped scarf in the college colours
clues: A maroon wool fibre with a green stripe, the college colours, is caught on the railings by the dormitory. The culprit wears a striped college scarf.
A couple hiding by the bell tower saw a striped college scarf wound up to someone's nose flash past. The culprit has a striped college scarf.

habits.label: Crosswords in ink
habits.habit: Does crosswords with a fountain pen
clues: In the senior common room a newspaper crossword is filled in in ink without a single blot, and the last word written is "raven". The culprit does crosswords with a fountain pen.
In the dean's office wastepaper basket there's a crumpled newspaper page with the crossword half done in fountain pen. The culprit does crosswords in ink.

habits.label: Argyle sweater vest
habits.habit: A knitted sweater vest with green diamonds
clues: A loop of green wool unravelled from a diamond knit is caught on the corner of the cabinet of stuffed animals in the zoology room. The culprit wears a knitted argyle vest.
The cloakroom attendant in the student club cellar remembered a green argyle vest under an open gown. The culprit has a knitted vest with green diamonds.

safe: Hale's references for scholarship candidates have vanished from the safe in the dean's office, and its door is locked on its combination. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The fireproof cabinet with the exam papers in the senior common room was opened without a single scratch, and the bundles are in the wrong order. The culprit knows the safe combination.
keys: The side door of the old library was kept locked all evening, yet the draught came from exactly there, and the lock was opened with a key. The culprit had keys.
The glass cabinet in the zoology room the raven was taken from is locked at night, and the lock hasn't been touched. The culprit had keys.
medic: Hale's cup in the old library has a sediment of sleeping draught, measured so that the reader could finish the last stanza. The culprit knows about poisons.
A jar of arsenical soap, used to treat skins for stuffing, is missing from the cabinet in the zoology room. The culprit knows about poisons.
tech: In the fuse box by the senior common room a fuse was replaced with a bodge, and the light in the library corridor goes out at a single flick of the switch. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The tape recorder in the student club cellar recorded all evening, and the last ten minutes have been cleanly erased, without clicks or breaks. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
tools: The stuffed raven in the zoology room was taken off its wooden stand: the screws were unscrewed without a single one stripped. The culprit is handy with tools.
The bell tower window, nailed shut since last winter, was freed of its nails and put back so that no gap shows. The culprit is handy with tools.
cash: The secret society's cash box in the student club cellar is empty, and the last page of the subscriptions book has been cut out with a razor. The culprit had access to money.
Hale's pocket holds crisp new notes from the bundle that lay in the dean's office in the morning for paying bonuses. The culprit had access to money.
passages: A passage behind a bookcase leads from the student club cellar to the old library, and the dust on the shelves has been disturbed. The culprit knows the service passages.
A walkway over the roof, which students aren't supposed to know about, leads from the bell tower to the dormitory attic, and there are fresh footprints on it. The culprit knows the service passages.
sched: According to the log, the dormitory is patrolled at eleven and at midnight, and someone crossed the courtyard exactly between them. The culprit knows the schedule.
The raven was taken during the hour when, by the timetable, the zoology room stands empty between the evening practical and the cleaning. The culprit knows the schedule.
quiet: The old library's floorboards creak at every step, yet someone reached Hale's armchair in the dark without anyone turning their head. The culprit moves silently.
The bell tower's spiral stairs boom like an empty barrel, yet the first-years smoking at the bottom didn't hear a step. The culprit moves silently.
strong: The bookcase hiding the passage to the student club cellar has been shifted, and its folios alone weigh a hundred kilos. The culprit is physically strong.
The hatch to the bell tower is weighed down by a cast-iron weight from the clock mechanism, and it was lifted and put back without any drag marks. The culprit is physically strong.
driver: The college's service estate car was moved from the garage to the dormitory's back entrance, and its bonnet is still warm. The culprit can drive.
There's a fresh tyre track on the muddy road to the bell tower, and the keys to the maintenance van hang on the wrong nail in the senior common room. The culprit can drive.
french: Baudelaire's translation, "Jamais plus", French for "Nevermore", is written in the margin of Hale's book in the old library. The culprit knows French.
A note to Hale was left in the senior common room: "Ce soir, vous lirez pour la dernière fois", French for "Tonight you read for the last time". The culprit knows French.
